page: Google Cloud Platform a3-highgpu-1g is an accelerator-optimized virtual machine engineered for GPU-intensive workloads, AI inference, and specialized compute pipelines. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor with 26 vCPUs across 13 physical cores running at a 2.7 GHz base clock, based on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU configuration provides 105 MB of L3 cache alongside advanced vector and matrix capabilities, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX tile extensions.

Hardware acceleration is anchored by a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU equipped with 80 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. Host memory is provisioned at 234 GB of RAM, establishing a high ratio of 9.0 GB per physical core. For high-throughput scratch data and pipeline caching, the instance includes an integrated 804 GB local NVMe SSD. Network configurations should note that zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Benchmark results highlight distinct performance boundaries across compute and machine learning operations. While single-core capabilities demonstrate strong execution—scoring 2,072 in Geekbench and 33.6 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression—multi-core throughput generally settles in the middle tier with a Geekbench multi-core score of 14,893 and a PassMark CPU score of 35,694. In language model execution, the single H100 GPU delivers 348.05 tokens per second for small 135M parameter models, but drops to 23.8 tokens per second on 7B models and 2.49 tokens per second on 70B models, illustrating the limits of running larger model footprints on a single accelerator.

In terms of resource efficiency, the a3-highgpu-1g balances entry into the Hopper architecture without the overhead of multi-GPU node deployments. It represents a targeted option for deep learning inference, model fine-tuning, image processing, and accelerated data transformations that fit comfortably inside an 80 GB GPU memory footprint.

The instance exhibits strong single-core performance alongside robust lightweight AI text generation, producing 348.05 tokens per second on 135M parameter models. However, multi-core throughput and larger 70B parameter inference reflect the constraints of a single-GPU allocation, yielding 2.49 tokens per second on heavy models. Without bundled public IPv4 networking, this machine provides an efficient single-accelerator environment for machine learning inference, computer vision, and specialized data engineering tasks.
